clue.text: Telephone receiver, a never-ending barrier

parts.note: to telephone someone is to ring them
a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: A clue listing the parts of a phone handset, then drifting off to an endless wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' looks like the part of the phone you hold, but here it is the dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring fence encloses an area completely, so the barrier has no end point.

clue.text: To create a fuss, bring up issue of opening pair

parts.note: to bring up a child is to raise it
Cain was the son of Adam and Eve, the first couple in Genesis

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a dispute over who opens the batting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening pair' suggests cricket's opening batsmen, but it is the first man and woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make trouble or kick up a loud protest.

clue.text: Inconsolable woman petrified

parts.note: in Greek myth a mother whose children were killed wept without end and was turned to stone, still weeping

explanation.surface: A grieving woman is frozen with fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petrified' suggests terrified, but in the myth she is literally turned to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this queen boasted of her children, lost them all to Apollo and Artemis, and became a weeping rock.

clue.text: Wastes fried food

definitions.meaning: squanders, as in frittering money away
pieces of fruit or vegetable dipped in batter and deep-fried

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means squanders time or money; the noun means battered, deep-fried morsels.

clue.text: Did it go to Falstaff's head when he hit the sack?

definitions.text: Did it go to Falstaff's head when he hit the sack?

parts.words: Did it go to Falstaff's head when he hit the sack?
parts.note: sack is the sherry Falstaff loved, so hitting the sack is drinking it, and also going to bed; a last drink before sleep might go to his head

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's drunken knight wonders whether drink went to his head as he went to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat, hard-drinking knight, and sack was his favourite wine. A cap also goes on the head at bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink taken just before bed, and also a cap once worn in bed.

clue.text: Queen to storm moving knight?

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
to storm is to rage or rant

explanation.surface: A chess player moves the queen to attack while a knight is moving.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture is the misdirection. A knight errant roamed in search of adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: A wandering knight roving in search of adventure is called a knight errant.

clue.text: Ancient Arabian region reveals Greek letter in gold case

indicators.note: the Greek letter sits inside the gold, as the clue says it is in it
the gold forms a case or shell wrapped around the Greek letter

parts.note: OR is the heraldic term for gold
phi is the twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An archaeologist announces that a gold casket from Arabia bears a Greek inscription.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold comes from heraldry and is a stock crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible names this land as the source of King Solomon's gold, and tradition places it in Arabia.

clue.text: Choice of work? Not I, being fixed

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: being fixed suggests the letters of Not I are put right in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a job offer, saying the choice is fixed and it will not be them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being fixed' rearranges NOT I into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternative one may pick from is a choice.

clue.text: The museum endowment allows many in

indicators.note: allows ... in says the endowment lets something inside it
completes allows in, letting a letter enter the endowment

parts.note: a heritage is something endowed or inherited
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: A museum's endowment fund admits lots of visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hermitage is the great art museum in St Petersburg, hence 'The museum'.
explanation.definitionFit: The State art gallery in St Petersburg, housed partly in the Winter Palace, is the famous museum meant.

clue.text: Railway child raised in Cumbrian village

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word for child is turned upward, read bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a child, a boy

explanation.surface: A railway child grows up in a village in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Cumbria is a county in north-west England, home to the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: This small Lake District village was Wordsworth's home at Rydal Mount.

clue.text: Club in Wigan centre for evening out

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club

indicators.note: the centre of the town name is its middle letter, the third of five

explanation.surface: Someone heads to a nightclub in Wigan, a northern English town, for a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening out' reads as a social night, but it means making cloth smooth and flat. Wigan is a town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes with a hot iron smooths away the creases, levelling the fabric.

clue.text: Red flag taken in and turned in

indicators.note: the word Red takes the synonym for flag inside itself

parts.note: to flag is to tire or weaken

explanation.surface: A red flag is lowered and handed in, perhaps at the end of a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning to grow weary. 'Turned in' means went to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has turned in has gone to bed for the night, which is one sense of retiring.

clue.text: Help one standing to a seat?

definitions.text: Help one standing to a seat?

parts.words: Help one standing to a seat?
parts.note: reads like offering a chair on a crowded bus, but the person standing is a candidate and the seat is in parliament, which voters can give them

explanation.surface: A courteous passenger offers their seat to someone left standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters choose a candidate for office, placing someone who stood for a seat into it.

clue.text: Soon getting out in test — result of a cutter?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the word for test

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: getting out suggests the letters of Soon are disturbed from their order

explanation.surface: Someone is told they will soon be out of an exam whose outcome depends on a cutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting out' scrambles the first word, and 'in' sets that inside the test. The cutter is a barber, so the adjective fits a haircut loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to barbers and haircutting, so a fresh trim is a barber's handiwork.

clue.text: Civic dignitary, male and ready to start possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way
to start means take only the opening letter of ready

explanation.surface: A town official is described as a man who is prepared to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' mixes MALE, AND and the R that 'to start' takes from 'ready'.
explanation.definitionFit: This senior councillor ranked just below the mayor in an English borough, a civic office of rank.

clue.text: Local target of river authority?

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon
a board is a governing authority

explanation.surface: A river authority is the target of local complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is the British word for a nearby pub, where darts are thrown at this.
explanation.definitionFit: The round target used in the pub game of darts hangs on many bar walls.

clue.text: Galsworthy piece, a hilarious thing when read backwards

indicators.note: the instruction to read backwards turns the whole phrase a hilarious thing end to end

parts.note: a gas is slang for something very funny

explanation.surface: Someone finds a Galsworthy novel very funny, but only when it is read from the end.
explanation.walkthrough: John Galsworthy wrote the Forsyte novels, gathered as a family chronicle. 'when read backwards' turns A GAS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Galsworthy's Forsyte novels form a long family chronicle, the kind of epic tale known by this name.

clue.text: Cleopatra's 18, receiving hip replacement and answering notes

indicators.note: the lover's name takes the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: 18 down is a lover; Cleopatra's was Mark Antony

indicators.note: replacement says the letters of hip are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Cleopatra's lover has a hip replacement while answering letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 18 down, a lover, so Cleopatra's is Mark Antony. 'replacement' scrambles the hip and 'receiving' sets it inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is music sung in alternating responses by two choirs, notes answering each other.

clue.text: But in the main, it is not tickled to death

definitions.text: But in the main, it is not tickled to death

parts.words: But in the main, it is not tickled to death
parts.note: the main is the open sea; poachers catch river fish by tickling them, but a fish living at sea escapes that fate

explanation.surface: Someone admits that, on the whole, they are not overjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as mostly and 'tickled to death' as delighted. Trout tickling is a poacher's trick of stroking a fish until it can be flipped out.
explanation.definitionFit: This trout migrates between sea and river, spending much of its life in salt water.

clue.text: Kept woman in standard affair

parts.note: par is the standard, as in golf or on par
an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: A mistress is caught up in a typical romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover or mistress, especially an illicit one, may be kept in luxury.

clue.text: Mean? On the contrary, jolly!

indicators.note: on the contrary is read as an instruction to turn the word On the other way round

parts.note: a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Someone asked if they are being mean protests that, quite the reverse, they are cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' looks like a stock phrase but makes NO, and 'jolly' is not cheerful but a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is an average or standard value, which is what a mean is in statistics.

clue.text: Ten years old, books are deteriorating

parts.note: a thing ten years old has lasted a decade
NT, the New Testament, is a group of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Ten-year-old books are falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: NT for the New Testament is a common crossword abbreviation for books.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in moral or cultural decline is degenerating, losing its former standards.

clue.text: Golf, an alternative requiring plenty of bottle

indicators.note: an alternative is another form, so the letters take another order

explanation.surface: Someone says golf is an option for those with plenty of nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for nerve, but here it is a real large bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bottle or jug for wine or beer holds plenty.

clue.text: Dark mild as ordered

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are arranged in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A drinker asks for a dark mild ale, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: Mild is a dark British beer, so the pub order is the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy and sombre, as a drab dark day is.

clue.text: Cant about one of the Brontes from a malicious publisher

indicators.note: the word for cant goes about, or around, the other pieces

parts.note: to cant is to tilt, and a ship that tilts is said to list
one is the Roman numeral I
the Bronte sisters first published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a hypocritical critic of a Bronte novel is a spiteful writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cant' suggests hypocrisy but means tilt. The Brontes wrote under the surname Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who publishes defamatory statements is a malicious writer of written slander.

clue.text: The French hail-and-farewell

parts.note: le is French for the
ave is Latin for hail, as in a greeting

explanation.surface: A Latin phrase of greeting and parting, rendered in French.
explanation.walkthrough: Ave atque vale, Latin for hail and farewell, is the phrase the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking one's departure is a goodbye, as in taking one's leave.

clue.text: His fabulous hard-top came first in spite of idling

definitions.text: His fabulous hard-top came first in spite of idling

parts.words: His fabulous hard-top came first in spite of idling
parts.note: the hard-top is the tortoise of his fable, which won the race against a hare that dawdled; the clue asks whose fable it is

explanation.surface: A classic hard-top car wins a race despite being left idling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard-top' suggests a car, but it is the shelled tortoise from the fable of the tortoise and the hare.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller told the fable in which the slow tortoise beats the boastful, napping hare.

clue.text: Rot like the bottom of a stump in the ground

indicators.note: the letter sits inside the ground, as a stump's base does

parts.note: soil is the ground

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A tree stump decays at its base where it sits in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literal: a stump's base is in the ground, and its last letter goes inside the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that rots goes bad, which is to go off or decay.

clue.text: Union backbiter may be full of it …

definitions.meaning: a blend or combination of things joined together

definitions.text: backbiter may be full of it
definitions.meaning: a back biter is a molar, a back tooth, which may be stuffed with a mercury dental filling

explanation.surface: A trade union official accuses a gossiping slanderer of being full of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backbiter' suggests a spiteful gossip, but it is a back tooth with a filling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a mixture or blend, and also the mercury alloy dentists use to fill teeth.

clue.text: Sherry, sadly, in bars is not opened…

indicators.note: not opened means the first letter is missing

parts.note: in bars of music, the Italian direction for playing sadly and mournfully

explanation.surface: Someone sadly reports that the sherry in the bars has not been opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bars' looks like pubs but means in written music, where the Italian marking for sadly is used.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dark, rich style of Spanish sherry from Jerez.

clue.text: … port brings me back to earth

indicators.note: back tells us the word me is read in reverse

parts.note: an earth is a fox's den or burrow

explanation.surface: A glass of port brings a dreamer back down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth' looks like the ground but is the home of a fox.
explanation.definitionFit: This German seaport lies on the Ems estuary near the Dutch border.

clue.text: Eleventh-hour recovery by the side

parts.note: the eleventh hour is the last moment, so late
a rally is a recovery, as in prices or health

explanation.surface: A sports team makes a last-minute comeback from the sidelines.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means sideways, moving or placed to one side.
